_meta.source: SkillsFuture Singapore, MySkillsFuture, MOE press releases and parliamentary replies on the SkillsFuture Level Up Programme
_meta.notes: Supplies the Long View ribbon. Its job is proportion: secondary school is the small band on the left. Markers are spaced at least four years apart so no two tap targets overlap at 375px. Several figures are provisional.

markers.title: I choose my subject levels
markers.body: The bit that feels enormous. It is adjustable, and students change levels every year.

markers.title: I sit the SEC
markers.body: One certificate, every subject and the level I took it at. First sat in 2027.

markers.title: After school starts
markers.body: JC, MI, poly, a foundation year or ITE. Every one of them has roads leading on.

markers.title: First real job, for most people
markers.body: By now nobody asks about my Sec 2 subjects. Within a few years they stop asking about the diploma too.

markers.title: SkillsFuture Credit is mine
markers.body: From 25, credit to spend on courses I pick. Not tied to an employer or to what I studied.

markers.title: A lot of people change direction
markers.body: Early switches are ordinary here. Work study routes exist so somebody can move without stopping work.

markers.title: The part nobody plans for
markers.body: Industries change under people. The ones who handle it are not those who chose right at fourteen.

markers.title: SkillsFuture Level Up
markers.body: At 40: a $4,000 credit, plus half my income as a monthly allowance while studying full time. Over 36,000 people used it in its first year, to April 2025.

markers.title: A subsidised diploma, at any age
markers.body: Up to 90 percent off a full time diploma at ITE, the polys, NAFA or LASALLE. People start in their forties and fifties.

markers.title: Still learning, still hiring
markers.body: Retirement and re employment ages keep rising. My working life will be longer than my parents' was.
